title: CAN RPG MAKER XP BE FULL SCREEN OR CHANGE WINDOW WIDTH AND HEIGHT TO 1920 X 1080?

posts.author: CoreFa
posts.body: Hi, I have been working in proyect for a long time, but i realised that most people got a 1920 x 1080 screen. So I need to change the game window to that resolution. If someone know about some script to change the width and height I would be infinitely grateful If this is too complicated, I would be grateful if you could talk to me by direct message to discuss further.. Thank you in advance.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
Welcome! It's good practice generally, on the Internet, to avoid big titles of all caps. It comes across as you shouting, and it's annoying to read.
CoreFa said:
i realised that most people got a 1920 x 1080 screen. So I need to change the game window to that resolution.
Click to expand...
I would suggest that is not a good reason to change your game window's size - you don't
need
to play fullscreen (no one does).
The layout of the game and its UI is designed to look good at a certain size - arbitrarily making your window several times larger without a plan for how to fill that space is much worse than simply playing the game in a window on the screen.
This is a screenshot from a game I saw recently - and keep in mind this was made in MZ, which starts off with a larger window and UI to begin with! It looks very amateurish, with maybe 70% of the screen real estate displaying nothing of interest, and was clearly sized up to 1920x1080 just because.
I'll let someone who's more familiar with the engine address the available scripts, although I can see from immediate Google results that they exist. I just wanted to make sure you're cognizant of the design portion.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
no, not directly.
RMXP's graphics library is closed source and has a hard limit of 640x480 (same as VX and VXA which use the same library)
You can use fullscreen which basically forces the windows size down to 640x480, or you can use external windows functions to zoom the 640x480 to the full screen size, but both require the internal game screen size to be 640x480
Alternatively you can switch to a display library project that was programmed a few years ago to make RMXP compatible to DirectX as that has no size limit.
Unfortunately I don't remember how that project was called.
